create.name: John Philip Newell
create.bio:
John Philip Newell is a teacher and writer on Celtic spirituality, born in Canada and also a Scottish citizen, who now makes his home with his wife Ali in the Findhorn ecovillage on the Moray coast. He earned his doctorate at the University of Edinburgh, was once Warden of Iona Abbey, and served for many years as a Church of Scotland minister before laying down his ordination in 2020, while still regarding himself as rooted in the Christian family. His more than fifteen books, among them Listening for the Heartbeat of God, Christ of the Celts, Sacred Earth Sacred Soul and The Great Search, return again and again to one idea: that Earth and every person carry something sacred.

In 2016 he founded Earth & Soul, through which he and his colleague Cami Twilling lead three-year cycles of retreats in North America and online, each built around one of his books and figures such as Pelagius, Brigid, Eriugena, John Muir or Etty Hillesum. With Ali he also hosts pilgrimage weeks on Iona that combine morning teaching, simple practice, chant in St Oran's Chapel and a walk around the island. His teaching joins scholarship with poetry and prayer, and it links inner awareness to care for the planet and for one another.

books.title: Sacred Earth, Sacred Soul: Celtic Wisdom for Reawakening to What Our Souls Know and Healing the World
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: Newell follows a line of Celtic voices from Pelagius and Brigid through Eriugena and the Carmina Gadelica to John Muir and Teilhard de Chardin. Each chapter draws out how that figure saw the sacred in the natural world and in every person, and what it might ask of us now.

books.title: The Great Search: Turning to Earth and Soul in the Quest for Healing and Home
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: Written for people whose spiritual lives no longer fit inside the church they grew up in, this book looks at nine figures, among them Thomas Berry, Nan Shepherd, Julian of Norwich, Rumi and Etty Hillesum. Through them Newell traces the deep longings he sees in people today, for vision, for closeness with the Earth and for presence.

books.title: Listening for the Heartbeat of God: A Celtic Spirituality
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: A short, readable introduction to the Celtic Christian stream, contrasting it with the more pessimistic strand of Western theology. Newell follows its thinkers and its prayer tradition through the centuries to show how it found the divine at the heart of life.

books.title: Christ of the Celts: The Healing of Creation
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: Newell reads the figure of Christ through Celtic eyes, as a revealer of the goodness already present in people and the natural world. The book weaves theology with stories and prayers from the Celtic tradition.

books.title: The Rebirthing of God: Christianity's Struggle for New Beginnings
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: Written partly from the ruins of Iona's old abbey, this book asks what may be emerging as Western Christianity declines. Newell suggests that a renewed sense of the sacred in all things can open conversation with other faiths and with the Earth.

books.title: Sounds of the Eternal: A Celtic Psalter
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: A prayer book of morning and evening prayers for each day of the week, drawing on Celtic and Jewish images of people made in the likeness of the divine. It is often used as the shared prayer book at his retreats.

books.title: Praying with the Earth: A Prayerbook for Peace
books.author: John Philip Newell
books.description: A week of daily prayers that draws together Jewish, Christian and Muslim scripture and imagery. The book is meant as a shared practice of praying for peace among the Abrahamic traditions.

courses.title: The Great Search 1
courses.description: A weekend retreat at Mercy Center Auburn in California, led with Cami Twilling and based on the first three chapters of The Great Search. It explores the search for wider vision, for closeness with the Earth and for spiritual presence, and can be taken on its own.

courses.title: The Fire of Hope 2
courses.description: The second retreat in his newest three-year series, held at the Bishop's Ranch in Healdsburg, California, with Cami Twilling. It turns to Thomas Merton, Joan Baez and Dr King as sources of inner strength, conscience and prayer.

courses.title: Iona Pilgrimage
courses.description: A pilgrimage week on the Isle of Iona with John Philip and Ali Newell, based at the St Columba Hotel. Days hold silent prayer, a morning teaching on Celtic wisdom, simple practices, evening chant in St Oran's Chapel and a walk around the island. Booking is made through the hotel.

courses.title: Sacred Earth Sacred Soul – An Online Retreat with John Philip Newell & Cami Twilling
courses.description: A two-hour online retreat, hosted by a community of Sisters of St Joseph, that pairs his teaching on the main themes of Sacred Earth Sacred Soul with practices led by Cami Twilling.

courses.title: Tending the Mother Fire
courses.description: A six-day retreat at Montreat Conference Center in North Carolina, named after the old Hebridean custom of never letting the hearth fire go out. He draws on prophetic voices from the Celtic world and beyond, and Cami Twilling leads the practices.

free_resources.title: Prayers and Meditations
free_resources.description: A page of short prayers he has written, including a Celtic version of the Lord's Prayer and a morning prayer of presence from his psalter. They can be read aloud alone or in a group.

free_resources.title: Threshold Community: A Guide to House Gatherings
free_resources.description: A free downloadable guide for small groups that meet at home or online to study his books, share practice and talk about action in the world.
